title: Applied ML Evals — Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, Quality Guardrails, and Regression Triage
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook defines the end-to-end applied-ML evaluation process used by Redwood Inference to onboard models, manage prompt sets and benchmarks, generate and validate quantization profiles, enforce quality guardrails, and triage regressions. It ties together the Eval Harness, prompt catalog, model onboarding checklist, quantization validation, and the regression triage workflow into a single operational reference.

Purpose

- Reduce time-to-production for new model variants while maintaining output quality and production SLOs.
- Ensure repeatable, automated evaluation and fast, prioritized human triage of regressions.
- Provide concrete thresholds, test artifacts, and owner responsibilities for each step.

Scope

Applies to: open and fine-tuned models evaluated for Redwood hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Includes models that will be: 
- Added to the model catalog
- Promoted to canary or general availability for serving

Roles and ownership

- Model Owner: engineering (model onboarding team) — primary contact for model integration and remediation.
- Eval Owner: applied-ml team — maintains eval harness, prompt set catalog, and automated pipelines.
- Perf Owner: serving-runtime — responsible for throughput/latency benchmarks and quant profiles.
- SRE/Oncall: eng-sre — monitors production SLOs and triggers regression triage when alerts fire.

Pre-requisites for onboarding

1) Model artifact and spec delivered to model-onboarding repo: architecture, tokenizer, expected max_seq_len, supported precisions.
2) CI integration: docker image or model descriptor in model-registry.
3) Baseline prompt sets selected (functional + safety + domain-specific).

Eval Harness Onboarding Checklist

1. Create eval config: include model_id, model_version, input_distribution, seed, and evaluation_shards. Example YAML snippet:

  eval_config:
    model_id: my-model-v1
    model_version: 2026-06-30
    input_distribution: production-sample-2026-06
    shards: 32
    metrics: [exact_match, rouge, bert_score, perplexity, response_latency_ms]

2. Add prompt sets: reference prompt-set IDs from the prompt catalog. Each prompt set MUST include metadata: owner, domain, intended-metric, and canonical_eval.
3. Run full eval in staging with fixed RNG and record artifacts (outputs, token-level traces, KV cache behavior). Command (eval harness):

  ./bin/eval-runner --config evals/my-model-v1.yaml --staging \
    --report-dir s3://redwood-evals/staging/my-model-v1/2026-07-15

4. Capture perf metrics: p50/p90/p99 latency per sequence-length bucket, tokens/sec, GPU utilization.

Prompt Sets & Benchmarking Guidance

- Prompt set format: JSONL with fields: id, prompt, expected_labels (optional), tags, difficulty, canonical_eval (boolean). Example line:

  {"id":"ps-qa-product-001","prompt":"What is the return policy?","tags":["customer_support","short"],"canonical_eval":true}

- Benchmarks should include at least three categories:
  1. Functional coverage (core task examples) — 500+ examples across buckets
  2. Edge cases (rare inputs, long context) — 200+ examples
  3. Safety and hallucination tests — 200 examples with adversarial prompts

- Acceptance criteria per prompt-set: baseline model must achieve minimum metric thresholds (used for gating promotion).

Acceptance thresholds (example):

  - Functional (accuracy/EM): >= 78%
  - ROUGE-L (summarization): >= 32
  - BERTScore: >= 0.78
  - Hallucination rate: <= 5%
  - Latency (p95) on target hardware: <= 300ms (short inputs)

Quantization Profiles and Validation

- Purpose: reduce inference cost while preserving quality. Each profile produced by perf team must include: target precision (int8/4-bit), per-layer quantization strategy (symmetric/asymmetric), calibration dataset, and validation results.

- Profile metadata (example):

  profile_id: qprofile-my-model-int8-2026-07
  precision: int8
  calibration_dataset: production-sample-2026-06-calib
  per_layer_strategy: [default, outlier-aware, per-channel]
  validation_eval_id: ev-2026-07-15-qv

- Validation steps:
  1. Run unit-level L1/Linf checks on activations vs fp16 baseline. Thresholds: L1 median ratio <= 1.05, max_abs_diff <= 2e-2 for softmax inputs.
  2. Run full eval harness with quantized model against canonical prompt sets. Quality delta thresholds: metric drop <= 2% absolute for primary metric, hallucination rate delta <= +1.5%.
  3. Perf/regression checks: tokens/sec improvement and GPU memory reduction reported.

Quality Guardrails and Automated Gating

- Automated pre-merge CI checks (eval-harness):
  - Smoke eval (50 examples) with canonical prompts must pass with no unexpected exceptions.
  - Metric regression detector: compares new model to baseline using bootstrap; fails if primary metric delta < -1.5% abs and p < 0.05.
  - Safety filter: any increase in harmful-response signals > 0.5% triggers manual review.

- Promotion gates (for canary/general availability):
  1. Canary: must satisfy functional thresholds, latency p95 target on canary infra, and no known safety regressions.
  2. GA: pass extended evals (full prompt catalog), quantized profile validation (if used), and business acceptance tests.

Regression Detection & Triage Playbook

1. Detection sources:
  - Continuous eval job alerts (eval-harness CI)
  - Production SLO alerts from Redwood Console (model-level SLO: p99 latency <= 600ms; error rate <= 0.5%)
  - Customer-reported incidents via support queue

2. Initial triage (within 60 minutes of alert):
  - Owner: SRE oncall acknowledges and tags incident: regression-type (quality/perf/safety).
  - Run quick-diff: compare failing request against last-known-good model using --trace-level token to identify divergence points.
  - If performance regression: collect flamegraphs and GPU metrics, escalate to perf owner.

3. Prioritization rubric:
  - P0: safety-critical regression or production outage (immediate rollback).
  - P1: severe quality regression affecting >5% of traffic or major customer impact.
  - P2: localized quality/perf regressions with mitigations.

4. Mitigation options:
  - Automated fallback to baseline model or previous variant (recommended first step).
  - Short-term routing rule: route affected customer(s) to Dedicated pool or alternative model.
  - Rollback: perform canary rollback following eng-deploy runbook.

5. Postmortem and action items:
  - Owner creates postmortem within 3 business days listing root cause, test gaps, and fixes.
  - Add new prompt cases to prompt catalog to cover regression examples.

Operational Runbook snippets

- Run a quick eval locally against a failing sample:

  ./bin/eval-runner --input sample-failure.jsonl --model-id my-model-v1 --trace-level token --staging

- Promote model to canary (automation):

  ./bin/promote-model --model my-model-v1 --version 2026-06-30 --stage canary --checks eval:pass,perf:pass

- Rollback command (emergency):

  ./bin/rollback-model --model my-model-v1 --to-version 2026-05-27 --force --notify oncall

Metrics and Dashboards to Monitor

- Eval dashboard: primary_metric_over_time, hallucination_rate, prompt_set_coverage, metric_delta_vs_baseline
- Perf dashboard: p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens_per_second, gpu_memory_used, queue_length
- Safety dashboard: flagged_responses_rate, policy_violations, adversarial_test_fail_rate

Reference artifacts to attach to onboarding ticket

- eval_config.yaml, prompt_sets (ids), quant_profile.json, perf_report.csv, sample traces (token-level), safety-report.html

Appendix — Example triage checklist

1. Acknowledge and classify. (SRE 0-60m)
2. Reproduce in staging with same input. (Eval Owner 60-180m)
3. Run diff vs baseline and identify divergence token index. (Model Owner 180-360m)
4. Apply mitigation (fallback/rollback/reroute). (SRE + Model Owner)
5. Create postmortem and add regression case to prompt catalog. (Model Owner)
